pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as one session covering strength, mobility and conditioning in 30-40 minutes, three to four times a week, plus short mobility protocols between calls at his desk. The prospect raised the rep's own number unprompted: 'I want to get at least five days, you know, four days I think is reasonable.' On the desk-break mobility work: 'Yeah, into it.' He had already pre-sold himself on the modality — 'I like the combination of mobility with weightlifting. I think that kettlebells cover both of that.'

Delivered as three variables with an eating window and no calorie counting, and tailored live to the trip he had just described — 'when you're traveling to Italy, and for example, after a good meal, you're gonna have a tiramisu, fine, have it.' The prospect accepted without engaging further. He had already set the terms himself: 'I'm not going to do this program if I have to change my life... I'm going to Italy this summer. I'm not going to not eat a dessert.' Worth noting he arrived pre-warned about exactly this promise from a previous vendor.

One-to-one design with Trevor, single app, video form checks, Trevor's private cell number, over-communication encouraged and programme adjustment around travel. The prospect's whole response was 'Yep. Sounds good to me.' This was the pillar aimed straight at his stated gap — 'I don't want to think' and 'there's nobody specialized' — and it drew the flattest reaction of the three, because the rep had not yet surfaced that gap when he presented it.

anchors.raw: I've actually been training, copying Trevor's videos from Instagram... otherwise I'm just going to his Instagram I'm clicking on a random video.
anchors.note: The most structurally interesting anchor in the batch. The programme's core movement content is already free, from the coach himself, and the buyer has been using it for two weeks. What he paid $6,000 for is sequencing and someone to think for him. The rep never named that distinction, which means the value story rests entirely on the prospect's own framing rather than the company's.

anchors.raw: You can hire a trainer anywhere. They all do the same . That's the problem. And there's no one really focused and specialized in something. And right now, in this moment, I want kettlebell.
anchors.note: The prospect devalued the substitute market himself and named specialisation as the scarce good. This is the single strongest supports-price anchor across the batch and the rep let it pass with 'I would say this is the most efficient way to train' rather than building on it.

anchors.raw: Yeah, I mean, that's probably what I'll do. I put everything on credit.
anchors.note: Removes cash-on-hand as a constraint entirely. Note the rep prompted it — 'Look, most guys just put it on credit' — rather than discovering it.

anchors.raw: that's another thing is like, I tried this program online, and they sold me on, you can still eat whatever you want
anchors.note: A trust anchor rather than a price one. He has been sold the exact nutrition promise before and it did not hold, which makes the identical promise a liability rather than an asset here. The rep delivered it anyway, unmodified, and the prospect did not react.

anchors.raw: I've done many online programs. I've done it all. I've done training since I'm 15 every day. Like I'm a seasoned guy
anchors.note: A history of paid online programmes that did not stick. No price was ever attached to any of them because the rep never asked, so his existing spend level on coaching is unknown.

unmet_demand.want: A way to train while travelling to a small Italian town with no gym and no kettlebell
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised it at length and solved it himself out loud — 'maybe I can buy a kettlebell in Italy and drive around with it... I haven't figured it out, but I'm going to figure.' The rep suggested an adjustable kettlebell, the prospect rejected it on baggage weight, and the thread was dropped. The programme demonstrably has travel workouts for exactly this case, and none was mentioned.

He asked directly — 'Is interest-free?' — and was told 'No, there is interest on this.' The in-house six-month option carries an implicit $1,200 premium over the upfront price, which is a cost he was never shown either.

unmet_demand.want: Assurance the programme is genuinely specialised rather than another generic trainer
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This was his stated buying criterion and the rep answered it with a personal anecdote — 'I was a gym rat for years and I switched to kettlebells like six years ago. I never came back to bench pressing' — rather than anything about Trevor's method, credentials or results. The programme almost certainly has that story; nobody told it.
